newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures closed for Japanese holiday.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures closed for Japanese holiday.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were not traded on Thursday due to a holiday in Japan. Trading will resume on Friday.

On Wednesday, the benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 35 points to close at 18,430 as initial market euphoria over the Japanese government's plans to boost the stagnant land market faded, dealers said.

They said there was speculation that the Finance Ministry's announcement on Tuesday that it would detail land liquidity measures on March 31 could just be an attempt to lift the Nikkei before the financial year end.
"The market welcomed the land scheme yesterday but there's some doubt about whether they can come up with a concrete plan in less than two weeks," said a trader with a Japanese house.
"But it was profit-taking rather than any aggressive selling," said the trader, adding that the June Nikkei was likely to be supported at 18,200.
He said the contract would face immediate resistance at 18,500 and at the more critical level of 18,700.
